papers.title: A new angle on matrix-vector complexity
authors: Cecilia Chen, Ethan N. W. Epperly, Michael W. Mahoney, Raphael A. Meyer, John Urschel
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2611.31955v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: The theory of worst-case matrix-vector complexity has been useful for guiding the design of fast linear algebra algorithms. However, there is a large theory-practice gap in the study of *one-sided* methods, which use matrix-vector products with $\mathbf{A}$ but not $\mathbf{A}^\top$. In practice, for fundamental problems like solving linear systems, one-sided methods like GMRES are often the fastest. By contrast, worst-case analysis often shows pessimistic results, for instance showing that one-sided methods cannot solve a linear system with ideal condition number 1 unless they read the whole matrix $\mathbf{A}$. Such worst-case complexity results do not reflect real-world experience.
